items.stem: Which TWO characteristics describe a good system requirement? (Select TWO.)

options.rationale: Correct: you must be able to confirm it is met.

options.text: It is traceable to a stakeholder need
options.rationale: Correct: traceability shows why the requirement exists.

options.text: It describes the detailed circuit design
options.rationale: That is design detail, not a system requirement.

options.text: It is written so loosely it cannot be tested
options.rationale: Untestable requirements are a defect, not a feature.

items.stem: A subsystem passes all its tests but the assembled system fails to meet the users' actual need. What has most likely gone wrong?

options.text: Verification succeeded but validation revealed the wrong thing was built
options.rationale: Correct: passing component tests is verification; meeting the real need is validation.

options.text: The requirements were perfect and nothing is wrong
options.rationale: A failed user need signals a validation gap.
Missing the user's need is a substantive failure.
A validation failure demands rework and re-examination of needs.
